title: Klio Clusters
description: Backups, WAL archiving and WAL restore of the PostgreSQL clusters backed up by Klio. Built from the Prometheus export of Klio's OpenTelemetry metrics.

options.content: *Namespace* is where the PostgreSQL cluster runs. *Cluster* lists every cluster that emits Klio plugin metrics, restore-only clusters included. *Instance* narrows the plugin panels to individual PostgreSQL pods.
Base backup lifecycle as seen by the plugin sidecar running in each PostgreSQL pod.

panels.title: Backups in progress
panels.description: Base backups currently running, per cluster.

panels.title: Successful backup runs
panels.description: Base backups completed successfully by the running clients sidecars, per cluster, over the selected time range.

panels.title: Failed backup runs
panels.description: Base backups that failed on the running clients sidecars, per cluster, over the selected time range.

panels.title: Backup run success ratio
panels.description: Fraction of base backup runs that succeeded over the selected time range (successful runs / total runs), per cluster.

panels.title: Latest backup duration
panels.description: Wall-clock duration of the most recent base backup, per cluster.

panels.title: Latest successful backup age
panels.description: Elapsed time since the most recent base backup completed successfully, per cluster. A value well above the backup interval means that cluster's backups have stopped succeeding.

panels.title: Latest failed backup age
panels.description: Elapsed time since the most recent base backup failure, per cluster. A small value means a failure happened recently.

panels.title: Latest backup start age
panels.description: Elapsed time since the most recent base backup started, per cluster. Compare against the latest duration to tell whether a backup is still running or overdue.

panels.title: Backup runs by outcome
panels.description: Base backup runs, grouped by cluster and outcome (success or failure).

panels.title: Failed backup runs by reason
panels.description: Failed base backup runs, grouped by cluster and failure reason.

panels.title: Backup duration percentiles
panels.description: 50th/90th/99th-percentile duration of successful base backup runs, per cluster.

options.content: Retention window of the physical PostgreSQL backups the Klio server keeps for each cluster.

panels.title: Retained backups
panels.description: Number of PostgreSQL backups currently retained per cluster and tier, with the Klio server that retains them.

panels.title: Oldest restorable point
panels.description: Timestamp at which the oldest retained PostgreSQL backup completed, per cluster and tier. It is the earliest point in time a restore can target, as long as all the WAL files since the backup started are still retained.

panels.title: Latest backup age (completion)
panels.description: Elapsed time since the most recently retained PostgreSQL backup completed, per cluster and tier.

panels.title: Latest backup age (start)
panels.description: Elapsed time since the most recently retained PostgreSQL backup started, per cluster and tier.

panels.title: Latest backup timeline
panels.description: PostgreSQL timeline of the latest retained backup, per cluster and tier. Differing from the oldest timeline means the retention window spans a promotion or failover.

targets.expression:
SELECT
  h0.cluster_name AS "Cluster Name",
  h0.tier AS "Tier",
  concat(CONV(h0.__value__, 10, 16), "/", CONV(l0.__value__, 10, 16)) as "start LSN",
  concat(CONV(h1.__value__, 10, 16), "/", CONV(l1.__value__, 10, 16)) as "end LSN"
FROM h0
JOIN l0 ON l0.cluster_name = h0.cluster_name AND l0.tier = h0.tier
JOIN h1 ON h1.cluster_name = h0.cluster_name AND h1.tier = h0.tier
JOIN l1 ON l1.cluster_name = h0.cluster_name AND l1.tier = h0.tier

panels.title: Latest backup LSN
panels.description: Start and end LSN of the latest retained PostgreSQL backup, per cluster and tier.

panels.title: Oldest backup age (completion)
panels.description: Elapsed time since the oldest retained PostgreSQL backup completed, per cluster and tier, reflecting each tier's effective retention horizon.

panels.title: Oldest backup age (start)
panels.description: Elapsed time since the oldest retained PostgreSQL backup started, per cluster and tier, reflecting each tier's effective retention horizon.

panels.title: Oldest backup timeline
panels.description: PostgreSQL timeline of the oldest retained backup, per cluster and tier. Differing from the latest timeline means the retention window spans a promotion or failover.

targets.expression:
SELECT
  h0.cluster_name AS "Cluster Name",
  h0.tier AS "Tier",
  concat(CONV(h0.__value__, 10, 16), "/", CONV(l0.__value__, 10, 16)) as "start LSN",
  concat(CONV(h1.__value__, 10, 16), "/", CONV(l1.__value__, 10, 16)) as "end LSN"
FROM h0
JOIN l0 ON l0.cluster_name = h0.cluster_name AND l0.tier = h0.tier
JOIN h1 ON h1.cluster_name = h0.cluster_name AND h1.tier = h0.tier
JOIN l1 ON l1.cluster_name = h0.cluster_name AND l1.tier = h0.tier

panels.title: Oldest backup LSN
panels.description: Start and end LSN of the oldest retained PostgreSQL backup, per cluster and tier.

options.content: Asynchronous operations the Klio server runs on the backups: tier-2 relay, verification and maintenance.

panels.title: Tier-2 backup relay attempts
panels.description: Total tier-2 relay attempts since the server last restarted, per cluster and outcome.

panels.title: Backup verification runs
panels.description: Total base backup verification checks since the server last restarted, per cluster, broken down by outcome and tier.

panels.title: Maintenance runs
panels.description: Total post-backup maintenance runs since the server last restarted, per cluster, tier and outcome.

options.content: WAL streamed by the client in the PostgreSQL pod, and written by the Klio server to each tier.

panels.title: WAL streaming timeline
panels.description: PostgreSQL timeline of the WAL streaming client.

panels.title: WAL block send duration percentiles (rate)
panels.description: 50th/90th/99th-percentile duration of the client's gRPC send of a WAL block to the server, per cluster. Reflects recent activity, over a rolling few-minute window.

panels.title: WAL block send duration percentiles (total)
panels.description: 50th/90th/99th-percentile duration of the client's gRPC send of a WAL block to the server, per cluster. Reflects all activity since the server last restarted.

panels.title: WAL timeline
panels.description: PostgreSQL timeline of the latest WAL written per cluster and tier

panels.title: Time since last WAL written
panels.description: Elapsed time since the server last wrote a WAL file for each cluster and tier.

targets.expression:
SELECT
  h0.cluster_name AS "Cluster Name",
  h0.tier AS "Tier",
  concat(CONV(h0.__value__, 10, 16), "/", CONV(l0.__value__, 10, 16)) as "written LSN"
FROM h0
JOIN l0 ON l0.cluster_name = h0.cluster_name AND l0.tier = h0.tier

panels.title: Latest written LSN
panels.description: Most recent WAL LSN the server has written for each cluster and tier

panels.title: WAL files written (rate)
panels.description: Rate of WAL files written by the server, split by cluster and storage tier.

panels.title: WAL files written (total)
panels.description: Total WAL files written by the server since it last restarted, split by cluster and storage tier.

panels.title: WAL bytes written (rate)
panels.description: Rate of WAL bytes written by the server, split by cluster and storage tier.

panels.title: WAL bytes written (total)
panels.description: Total WAL bytes written by the server since it last restarted, split by cluster and storage tier.

panels.title: WAL tier-2 upload duration percentiles (rate)
panels.description: Percentile duration of the tier-2 archival upload to remote storage, per cluster. Reflects recent activity, over the rate interval window.

panels.title: WAL tier-2 upload duration percentiles (total)
panels.description: Percentile duration of the tier-2 archival upload to remote storage, per cluster. Reflects all activity since the server last restarted.

options.content: How far the WAL stored in tier 1 and tier 2 trails behind the PostgreSQL primary.

panels.title: Tier-1 replication lag (bytes)
panels.description: Byte distance between the primary's current WAL LSN and the LSN Klio's streaming client has written to disk and flushed.

panels.title: Tier-1 replication lag (seconds)
panels.description: Time between a commit on the primary and Klio's streaming client writing to disk and flushing the corresponding WAL.

panels.title: Tier-2 archival lag (bytes)
panels.description: Bytes difference between the WALs in tier 1 and tier 2 per cluster.

options.content: WAL files the plugin serves to PostgreSQL during recovery or on a replica, per instance.

panels.title: WAL restore duration percentiles (rate)
panels.description: 50th/90th/99th-percentile time PostgreSQL waited on the plugin for each successfully restored WAL file, per instance (pod). It covers the plugin serving the request, not the replay that follows nor prefetch downloads that finished in the background. Prefetch hits (a local rename) and misses (a wait on a download) are pooled, so with a high hit ratio the misses only show in the upper percentiles; see the prefetch hit ratio and wait share panels for their weight. Reflects recent activity, over the rate interval window.

panels.title: WAL restore duration percentiles (total)
panels.description: 50th/90th/99th-percentile time PostgreSQL waited on the plugin for each successfully restored WAL file, per instance (pod). It covers the plugin serving the request, not the replay that follows nor prefetch downloads that finished in the background. Prefetch hits (a local rename) and misses (a wait on a download) are pooled, so with a high hit ratio the misses only show in the upper percentiles; see the prefetch hit ratio and wait share panels for their weight. Reflects all activity since the plugin sidecar last restarted.

panels.title: WAL restores (rate)
panels.description: Rate of WAL restores served by the plugin to PostgreSQL, per instance (pod), split by the tier that served them and by outcome. not_found is PostgreSQL asking for a WAL that was never archived, the routine end-of-archive signal rather than an error.

panels.title: WAL restores (total)
panels.description: Total WAL restores served by the plugin to PostgreSQL since the plugin sidecar last restarted, per instance (pod), split by the tier that served them and by outcome.

targets.expr: 1 - sum by (cluster_name, k8s_pod_name) (rate(klio_plugin_wal_restore_duration_nanoseconds_count{outcome="success",cache_hit="false",k8s_namespace_name=~"$namespace",cluster_name=~"$cluster",k8s_pod_name=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (cluster_name, k8s_pod_name) (rate(klio_plugin_wal_restore_duration_nanoseconds_count{outcome="success",k8s_namespace_name=~"$namespace",cluster_name=~"$cluster",k8s_pod_name=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: WAL restore prefetch hit ratio
panels.description: Fraction of successful WAL restores served straight from the prefetch spool instead of waiting on a download, per instance (pod). A falling ratio means prefetch is not keeping pace with PostgreSQL replay.

panels.title: WAL restore wait share
panels.description: Fraction of wall-clock time PostgreSQL spent waiting on the plugin for WAL files, per instance (pod). The rest of the time goes to replaying the restored WAL and to starting each restore_command, which the restore duration does not include, so the restore rate is set by replay, not by the restore duration. Near 0% recovery is limited by replay; a high share means PostgreSQL is waiting on downloads.
